input.quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
input.rationale: The only licence-responsive provision is p0346, and it is an express refusal to license: the Servicer "will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party." Searches for "license", "grant", "right to use", "software" and "irrevocable" surface nothing else in our favour: the other hits are regulatory qualification licences and security-interest "Grants" (defined at p0763 as a pledge, not an IP licence). The power of attorney at p0105 runs from the Issuer to the Servicer and is revocable by us, so it benefits our side and is not flagged. With no grant at all, our Affiliates are excluded with no path to add them and nothing is transferable to a successor, so the clause fails both fallback elements and sits in walk-away territory. We convert the disclaimer sentence into a licence to the Issuer at the fallback level (Affiliates on written notice; transferable to an M&A successor) and keep the retained carve-out for confidentiality- and law-restricted materials verbatim so no contradictory mechanic survives. The preferred perpetual/irrevocable, subscription-termination and contractor elements are not pursued, as this servicing structure has no paid-up or subscription licence construct.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Convert the Servicer's express refusal to license servicing software into a licence to the Issuer, extended to Issuer Affiliates on written notice and transferable to an M&A successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement gives us no licence to the Servicer's servicing software, models and processes and expressly disclaims one, so servicing cannot be continued on a servicer transition. We have replaced that disclaimer with a licence to the Issuer covering our Affiliates on written notice and transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition (our fallback position), while preserving the existing carve-out for materials restricted by confidentiality or by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.

ops.oldText: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
ops.newText: The Servicer grants the Issuer a license to use its processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications to service the Receivables, which license extends to the Issuer's Affiliates on written notice to the Servicer and is transferable to any successor to the Issuer by merger or acquisition; provided that the Servicer need not provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
